subject: Performance MAP & quant/kernel benchmarking — proposed plan and milestones
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@brighthealth.com>, BrightHealth Platform Team <platform@brighthealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance MAP & quant/kernel benchmarking — proposed plan and milestones

Hi Elena / BrightHealth team,

Thanks for the sync today — per our conversation I put together a short mutual action plan focused on performance benchmarking (latency, throughput, TTFT) and the quantization/kernel profile matrix we'll run during evaluation. Goal: give you a clear decision path for whether to enable INT8/INT4 quantized variants for production traffic and a safe canary timeline.

High-level asks / constraints from you:
- p95 latency target: <= 200ms for interactive endpoints
- TTFT target: <= 30ms for first token
- Allow up to 4x concurrency per session in peak tests
- Any data retention or audit constraints we should embed in runs? (log redact level)

Proposed benchmark matrix (we'll provide scripts + seeded prompts):
1) Precision baseline: FP16 and BF16 (reference)
2) Quantized: INT8 (per-channel symmetric) and INT4 (experimental) via our XQuant pipeline
3) Kernels: torch_cuda_fused_attn_v2, fastkv_kv_cache_v1, int8_dotprod_avx512 (where applicable)
4) Seq lengths: 128 / 512 / 2048
5) Concurrency tested: 1 / 4 / 8 / 16 (measure p50/p95/p99, throughput tokens/s, TTFT)
6) Regression checks: generation-quality sampling (n=100), perplexity delta threshold, and output-stability sampling hashes

Milestones (proposed):
- Aug 11: Benchmark runs complete (Redwood)
- Aug 12: Internal signal review + recommendation (Redwood eng)
- Aug 13: MAP decision meeting (features to enable for canary)
- Aug 25: Canary rollout (BrightHealth canary)
- Oct 01: GA across production routes (target)

Deliverables we will provide:
- Consolidated perf report (PDF) + raw CSVs
- Kernel-level flame/ops breakdown and regression summary
- Suggested runtime routing policy: FP16 default / INT8 warm-batch / INT4 offline-only (if viable)

If that looks good I'll send the scripts and schedule the Aug 12 internal review. Also: anything else we should measure (memory usage, cache eviction events, etc.)?

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Performance MAP & quant/kernel benchmarking — proposed plan and milestones

Thanks Soojin — this looks exactly like what we need. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We must keep p95 <= 200ms for customer-facing flows (billing check-ins & claims help).
- We can tolerate slightly higher p99 for background jobs.
- Please include memory footprint/peak GPU RAM for each precision; we have strict node packing targets.
- For INT4 please note: procurement will want a short note on fallback behavior if generation quality regresses.

Also attaching a sanitized config and a small sample prompt set that matches our live traffic distribution. We'll need the runs to exclude PHI and to keep logs redacted to the transaction_id level.

ATTACHMENT: BH_prompt_sample_v3.json (1.1MB)
ATTACHMENT: BH_prod_config_sanitized.yaml (2KB)

We are available for the Aug 13 decision meeting; please send calendar invite.

—Elena
Elena Ramos

BrightHealth

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@brighthealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance MAP & quant/kernel benchmarking — proposed plan and milestones

Elena / Soojin — quick technical notes from the infra side: 

1) Test matrix refinement: run each precision across seq lengths 128/512/2048 and batch-concurrency combos {1x1, 4x1, 8x1, 16x1} where the first is concurrent sessions and second is per-request batch size. Aim to capture both low-latency single-user and high-throughput burst scenarios.

2) Metrics to capture (we'll emit these to the CSV): p50/p95/p99 latency (step-level and total), TTFT (server-side), throughput tokens/sec, GPU util %, GPU memory peak, kernel time breakdown (ms per kernel).

3) Kernel profiling: enable nvtx segments for fused_attn, kv_cache, matmul, and quant_dequant ops. We'll capture per-kernel histograms and operator counts; export as quant-kernel-results.csv.

4) Regression checks: sample 200 outputs and compute BLEU/ROUGE and embedding-distance to baseline FP16. If embedding-distance > 0.12 or ROUGE drop > 1.5 we flag as regression. We'll also run token-level divergence sampling with fixed seeds.

5) INT4 note: INT4 paths are experimental — on long contexts (>=2048) we saw instability on very large batches in our internal runs due to low-precision accumulation in int4_dotprod kernels. We'll try a patched int4_dotprod_v2 but expect occasional quality variance. Recommend: enable INT4 only for offline/analytics or tight-cost experiments unless team accepts a small quality delta.

Action: I'll push the benchmark scripts and the Docker image hash to the git link (https://git.redwood.ai/bench/brighthealth-perf-scripts) by EOD today.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Lead, Inference Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@brighthealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance MAP & quant/kernel benchmarking — proposed plan and milestones

Elena / team — attaching the final consolidated report after internal review. Key highlights (top-line):

Summary of results (interactive endpoint, seq=512, concurrency=4):
- FP16 (baseline): p50=28ms, p95=112ms, TTFT=15ms, throughput=850 tok/s
- BF16: comparable to FP16 within +/-3% across metrics
- INT8 (XQuant, per-channel): p50=32ms, p95=140ms, TTFT=19ms, throughput=1200 tok/s (higher batch throughput on burst jobs)
- INT4 (experimental): p50=40ms, p95=220ms (regression on heavy long-context runs), TTFT=28ms, throughput=1600 tok/s for high-batched offline runs but observed quality drift on some prompts

Kernel-level notes:
- torch_cuda_fused_attn_v2 accounts for ~42% of token time on FP16; int8_dotprod_avx512 reduces matmul wall-time by ~25% in INT8 runs, but increases int->fp accumulation overhead in some long sequences.
- fastkv_kv_cache_v1 consistently reduced KV cache overhead at high concurrency (8+) across precisions.

Recommendation:
- Production interactive endpoints: keep FP16 (or BF16) as default to preserve quality and predictable p95.
- Warm-path batching: enable INT8 for batched background and scheduled jobs where slightly higher p95 is acceptable and throughput gains matter.
- INT4: keep in experimental channel only; require additional sampling and migration gates before any canarying to production.

Regression checks: embedding-distance and ROUGE remained within thresholds for INT8; INT4 triggered 2.8% of sampled prompts beyond the ROUGE threshold (need mitigation).

Next steps / asks for BrightHealth:
1) Confirm you accept the recommended routing policy and the Aug 25 canary window.
2) Confirm the redaction level for logs (transaction_id OK?).
3) Approve procurement of one extra A100-class instance if you want to run INT4 safe-path.

ATTACHMENT: BrightHealth_MAP_PerfBench_v1.pdf (final)
ATTACHMENT: quant-kernel-results.csv

Thanks — happy to walk through the PDF on the call.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

We approve the Aug 25 canary window and will schedule the procurement for one extra A100 node (procurement lead copied). Please add the Redwood run artifacts to our shared drive and send the calendar invite for Aug 13 decision meeting (we'd like a 30 min slot).

Thanks,
Elena
